correctness.rationale: The dual contains the full two-skeleton, connected-four-set tetrahedra and five-cycle four-simplices. If all four-subsets of a five-set are connected, the set is connected and cannot be a tree (delete a nonleaf), so it induces C5. Six such five-subsets would give 4e=30. In a star the three-leaf triangle has a unique completion, since a second common neighbor creates a square. In a path the triangle comprising an end and the disjoint end edge has a second completion exactly in a pentagon; it has at most two completions globally, by the no-square condition. Thus the pentagon tetrahedron incidence cycle along these triangles is isolated from other blocks. Removing a four-simplex and one private facet opens that cycle, then free-triangle collapses remove the four remaining facets; off-cycle tetrahedra have private triangles. The residual dual is simply connected and two-dimensional, with free H_2 of rank μ by Euler characteristic. The six-set obstruction makes the primal simply connected for n≥9. Integral Alexander duality concentrates the primal homology in degree n−5; Hurewicz and homological Whitehead give the wedge including the zero-rank case. Paths and stars are counted once by middle edge and center, respectively. The independent bounded check enumerated exact incidences and collapse schedules in C5 with four isolates, two disjoint C5s, and two C5s joined at a single vertex, obtaining (n,c4,p5,μ) = (9,5,1,52), (10,10,2,76), (9,22,2,36). No frozen script was run.
residual_risks: The independent check was restricted to three examples; the reported 300 generated runs were not reproduced. Correctness for all graphs and over the integers rests on the collapse and duality argument.
